$comment: SOURCE, NOT GENERATED. Hand-written notes for the changelog, keyed by version, plus `unreleased` for work that has no version yet. Everything else on that page is derived from git, which is the right way round for drawings: a list of what was added or redrawn should never be typed. But a release is not always drawings. The corner treatment added a whole axis without adding a name, so git had nothing to report and the page would have announced 48 redraws and nothing else. Write a note only where the release did something a count cannot describe, and keep it to two or three sentences: this sits above the tiles, not instead of them. Entries here are never edited once published, for the reason `pipeline/README.md` gives about the changelog only ever growing. Plain prose: neither the page nor the Paper board renders markdown, so a backtick arrives as a backtick.
unreleased: Every drawing now comes in a second corner treatment. Sharp is the same icon with its fillets removed and its caps squared, so the set holds twice the SVGs under the same names, and picking it is a switch in the browser rather than a different library. It travels the way the styles do: its own entry points in the React package, a corners flag on the CLI, and sharp leading the path in the registry.
